messages:
frank: heads-up — bringing up horizon-stitch-13b (q4f) with a staged speculative decode flow on a small fleet. goal: 2x token throughput w/ <10% quality delta on our convo/evals. initial quick numbers below, need eyes on eval methodology and config choices.

frank: quick bench command i ran locally:
```
# micro-bench (reuse bench harness)
python tools/bench_decode.py --model horizon-stitch-13b-q4f \\n  --spec-stage fast_prob=0.65,confirm_prob=0.35 \\n  --seq 512 --warm 100 --iters 300 --temp 0.7 --top_p 0.9
```
frank: rough outputs (median over 3 runs):
- baseline (no spec): 18.4 tok/s, median lat 42.1ms, ppl 12.3
- spec (fast_prob=0.65): 37.6 tok/s, median lat 41.3ms, ppl 12.8
- effective speedup ~2.04x token throughput, latency median ~flat, quality delta ~-0.6% (nat eval), QA exact-match drop ~1.8pp

mira: nice numbers. couple of questions: 1) what's the eval set for "nat eval"? 2) are you measuring with identical RNG seeds / sampling params? 3) which decodes are counted as "confirmed" vs fast?

frank: answers — nat eval = combined convo-naturalness set (conv_nat_v2, ~3k prompts). seeds fixed across runs. by "confirmed" i mean tokens produced in the confirm stage (we re-run a slower scorer on candidate token prefixes and accept/reject). fast stage is pure sampling at small beam.

devon: curious — what's the fast/confirm policy exactly? is it probability threshold on token logit gap or a learned critic?

frank: current probe uses a simple KL/entropy heuristic on the distribution at each step: if entropy < 2.1 or top1_prob > 0.55, we accept fast token, otherwise push to confirm. simple, interpretable.

mira: can you share the prompt distribution breakdown? convo vs docs vs code? spec will hit them very differently.

frank: breakdown: convo 60%, docs 25%, code 15%. i agree — code paths show higher regression risk.

ops-bot: @frank deploy-job horizon-stitch-q4f-specict started on infra-qpool-3 (job id: 0x7f3a2) :gear:

frank: pasted a short log from the cluster run (trimmed):
```
[run 1] seq512 iters300: tokens/sec=36.8, median_lat=43.2ms, nat_score=87.2
[run 2] seq512 iters300: tokens/sec=38.4, median_lat=40.7ms, nat_score=86.9
[run 3] seq512 iters300: tokens/sec=37.6, median_lat=41.3ms, nat_score=86.8
avg nat delta vs baseline = -0.62%
QA EM on SQuAD-like holdout: baseline 79.4 -> spec 77.6 (-1.8pp)
```

mira: that's consistent with what we worried about. can you pull a few failure cases? i expect hallucination rate on multi-hop Qs to increase. also, did you try lowering fast_prob to 0.5?

frank: grabbed 3 failing QA examples and added to gist: https://redwood.gists/frag/hst-spec-qa-fails (contains prompts + baseline vs spec outputs). i'll run ablation on fast_prob 0.5 and 0.75 next.

devon: i'll run a controlled ablation matrix tomorrow: fast_prob in [0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8], entropy thresholds [1.8,2.1,2.5], keep seed fixed. will log with bench harness and output per-domain breakdown.

mira: also add a calibration check: run spec decode but force confirm on first N tokens to see prefix-sensitivity (we saw this breakage in past models).

frank: good call — adding confirm_first=4 to the matrix.

sre-bot: deploy complete on infra-qpool-3 for job 0x7f3a2 :white_check_mark:

devon: will push results as csv + small summary tomorrow. if we can get speedup >1.8x with <=1% nat delta and <=1pp QA EM drop that's a green signal for canary. otherwise we need either a smaller fast_prob or move to a two-pass confirm (fast->nucleus rescoring).

mira: agreed. thanks all — particularly want to review the failure gist before any canary. @devon ping me when you have the matrix done. :eyes:
